land.text: Syria as drawn by Cliopatria's 'Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party' row (1967-1972), the same cells as this row's 1973 shape

predecessors.note: Not a new state: Cliopatria's row boundary between 1972 and 1973. The republic-of-syria dossier (me-10-k) already treats republic-of-syria, arab-socialist-ba-ath-party and syria as one state.

capitals.name: Damascus
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital and largest city: Damascus.' Coordinates from the gazetteer's place list.

correction.text: Syria in its pre-war line with the Golan Heights (the 1963-1966 shape, 187,924 km2); the Golan stays Syria's land under Israeli occupation until the annexation law of 14 December 1981

keyframe_review.note: 185,909 km2 for 1973-1975 against the infobox's 185,180 km2 (ratio 1.00; the page gives no year for the figure). The shape is Syria without the Golan (the gazetteer's Golan region has 0 cells in it, 9 of 10 in Cliopatria's Israel shape). The predecessor dossier (arab-socialist-ba-ath-party, me-10-k) keeps the Golan inside Syria under the occupation hatch, and so does this one: 'the Israel Defense Forces captured the Golan Heights on [9-10 June]' (1967), 1,070 km2 of the Heights proper and 100 km2 of the Mount Hermon slopes. The occupation event carries the hatch; the Yom Kippur War of October 1973 and the 1974 agreement are in the ledger.

correction.text: Syria with the whole Golan for 1976 to 1981, the Syrian-held part of the Heights being Syria's and the rest under Israeli occupation (hatched by the ledger) until the Golan Heights Law of 14 December 1981

keyframe_review.note: 186,623 km2 (ratio 1.01 to the infobox). This Cliopatria shape holds 3 of the Golan's 10 cells (the part restored to Syria by the 1974 agreement: 'Civil administration of a third of the Golan Heights, including the capital Quneitra, was restored to Syria in a disengagement agreement the year after the 1973 Yom Kippur War') and gives 6 to Israel. Corrected to the pre-war line with the whole Golan for 1976-1981, as for 1973, because Israel's annexation law dates only from 14 December 1981 ('Although the law effectively annexed the territory to Israel, it did not explicitly spell out a formal annexation'); from 1982 see syria_1982. Lebanon: the Syrian army entered on 31 May 1976 (ledger), which this shape does not show.

correction.text: Syria after the 1981 annexation: Cliopatria's 1983 shape, with the Quneitra area restored in 1974 and without the Heights held and annexed by Israel

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1982 alone: Cliopatria's next shape starts in 1983, but the Golan Heights Law of 14 December 1981 had already taken the Israeli-held Golan out of Syria's control ('effectively annexed the territory'). The shape is Cliopatria's 1983 shape (Syria with the Quneitra part of the Golan restored in 1974).

186,700 km2 for 1983-1986 against 185,180 km2 (ratio 1.01). Nothing on the pages opened moves Syria's border between 1982 and 2010: the Syrian army in Lebanon is an occupation (ledger), not a change of frontier. The 77 km2 difference from the 1976 shape is digitising noise.
186,623 km2 for 1987-2005 (ratio 1.01). Unchanged frontier; the Syrian presence in Lebanon (31 May 1976 to 30 April 2005) is carried by the occupation events, not by the shape.

186,752 km2 for 2006-2013 (ratio 1.01). The shape holds 4 of the Golan's 10 cells against 3 in 1987: a 129 km2 digitising difference, not a border event. It is the best whole-country outline Cliopatria has and is used below as the sovereign shape for 2014-2024.

correction.text: the whole of Syria as in Cliopatria's 2006 shape; the zones held by the opposition, the Islamic State, the Kurdish-led administration and Turkey are taken out by the ledger from 2012 on

keyframe_review.note: 118,734 km2 for 2014-2023 against 185,180 km2 (ratio 0.64, inside the factor of two but a different thing): the shape is the government-held part: it drops 64,490 km2 of the 2013 shape, 60,190 km2 of it inside the 68,889 km2 outline (across Syria, Iraq and Turkey) that Cliopatria also files under the row 'Mujahideen' (2014-2024; the mujahideen dossier finds that outline unrelated to the Afghan mujahideen and leaves it to a Syrian dossier). It is frozen for ten years, whereas the page has the front move every year: ISIS held 'roughly two-thirds of Syria by May 2015', the government 'about two-thirds of the country' by 2021 and the opposition 'roughly 30%' in early 2023. Corrected to the whole country; the ledger takes the rebel-, ISIS-, SDF- and Turkish-held zones out year by year (loss/gain and occupation events).

correction.text: the whole of Syria; the government that holds it changes on 8 December 2024 but the land does not

keyframe_review.note: 118,734 km2, the 2014 outline repeated. On 8 December 2024 'Opposition forces captured the capital Damascus' and the Assad government fell; the state continues (ledger rename) and the Syria page does not give a changed frontier. Corrected to the whole country for the same reason as syria_2014; Israel's entry into the buffer zone on the Golan in December 2024 is an occupation event.

region.text: Syria with Damascus as capital and the Golan inside its pre-war line

ledger.note: 1973: Cliopatria's 'Syria' row begins over the cells of its Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party row; the Syrian Arab Republic has stood since the end of the French mandate ('17 April 1946', infobox) and this is a row boundary, not a founding. The Syria page dates nothing in 1973 but the October war ('On 6 October 1973, Syria and Egypt initiated the Yom Kippur War against Israel').

region.text: the Golan Heights proper (1,070 km2) and the slopes of Mount Hermon (100 km2)

ledger.note: Carried over from the predecessor dossier: Israel has held the Golan Heights since June 1967 ('the Israel Defense Forces captured the Golan Heights on [9-10 June]'; 1,070 km2 of the Heights proper and 100 km2 of the Hermon slopes). The year 1973 is this dossier's start, not the page's date.

region.text: the Golan Heights, where Syrian forces overran the southern part

ledger.note: 6 October 1973: Syria and Egypt attack Israel and the Golan front opens. 'The war started on 6 October 1973, when the Arab coalition launched a surprise attack'; 'Syrian forces gained territory in the Golan Heights' before Israel 'pushed most of the Syrians back to the Purple Line'. The Golan page: 'Syrian forces overran much of the southern Golan, before being pushed back by an Israeli counterattack.'

region.text: the Golan front and the Bashan salient held by Israel at the ceasefire

ledger.note: 25 October 1973: the fighting ends. 'A second ceasefire on 25 October officially ended the conflict.' At the ceasefire (infobox) 'Israeli forces held 500 km2 of the Syrian Bashan region of the Golan Heights' beyond the Purple Line; the disengagement agreement that returned ground followed in 1974 (next event).

region.text: a third of the Golan Heights, including the capital Quneitra

ledger.note: 1974: Quneitra returns to Syria. 'Civil administration of a third of the Golan Heights, including the capital Quneitra, was restored to Syria in a disengagement agreement the year after the 1973 Yom Kippur War.' The page is not consistent on the year of the return: 'In 1975, following the 1974 ceasefire agreement, Israel returned a narrow demilitarized zone to Syrian control' (the buffer zone is 266 km2). The month of the agreement is not on the pages opened.

region.text: northern and eastern Lebanon (the Beqaa and the north)

ledger.note: 31 May 1976: the Syrian army enters Lebanon. 'On May 31, 1976, the Syrian Army invaded Lebanon with 2,000 troops and 60 tanks in a three-pronged offensive'; infobox 'Syria occupies northern and eastern Lebanon'. The page names the Beqaa valley (north through it, then west towards Tripoli) and halts the other columns at Beirut and Sidon; the provinces are the reading of the infobox.

region.text: central Lebanon

ledger.note: October 1976: Syria takes central Lebanon. 'A second Syrian offensive in mid-October 1976 succeeded at capturing all of central Lebanon.' Mount Lebanon is the reading of 'central Lebanon'. On 13 October 1990 'the Syrian forces attacked and occupied the Presidential Palace at Baabda', inside the same province.

region.text: the Golan Heights held by Israel, less the Quneitra area restored in 1974

ledger.note: 14 December 1981: Israel passes the Golan Heights Law, ending the military occupation of the Golan in favour of annexation. 'On 14 December 1981, Israel passed the Golan Heights Law', extending 'laws, jurisdiction and administration'; the Quneitra part restored in 1974 stays Syrian.

region.text: the Golan Heights held by Israel

ledger.note: 14 December 1981: Israel annexes the Golan. 'Although the law effectively annexed the territory to Israel, it did not explicitly spell out a formal annexation.' Syria and the UN reject it; the map shows the land as Israeli.

region.text: northern and eastern Lebanon

ledger.note: 30 April 2005: Syria completes its withdrawal from Lebanon. 'Syria completed its full withdrawal from Lebanon on 30 April 2005' (infobox '31 May 1976 - 30 April 2005'), after the Cedar Revolution and Bashar al-Assad's announcement of 5 March 2005. The Syria page: 'In 2005, Syria ended its military presence in Lebanon.'

region.text: central Lebanon

ledger.note: 30 April 2005: Syria leaves central Lebanon as well (same sentence).

region.text: the Jazira sub-region of the Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria

ledger.note: 2012: the Kurdish-led autonomous region takes shape in the north-east. 'The region gained its de facto autonomy in 2012 in the context of the ongoing Rojava conflict'; its sub-regions are 'Afrin, Jazira, Euphrates, Raqqa, Tabqa, Manbij and Deir Ez-Zor'. The page does not say which land was held in 2012; Hasakah (the Jazira) is the reading.

region.text: the regional capital Raqqa

ledger.note: 2013: rebels take Raqqa. The war page's lead: the rebels' successes included 'capturing the regional capitals of Raqqa in 2013 and Idlib in 2015'. The Islamic State page: 'Raqqa in Syria was under IS control from 2013 and in 2014 it became the group's de facto capital city.'

region.text: Eastern Syria: Raqqa and Deir ez-Zor

ledger.note: 2014: the Islamic State takes eastern Syria. 'In 2014 ISIS was able to seize control of large parts of Eastern Syria'; the Islamic State page has the caliphate declared on 29 June 2014 with Raqqa as its de facto capital. Reviewer me-10-l: confidence lowered to 2, the Syria page says 'large parts of Eastern Syria' and names neither Raqqa nor Deir ez-Zor.

region.text: the regional capital Idlib

ledger.note: 2015: rebels take Idlib, the second provincial capital they win ('capturing the regional capitals of Raqqa in 2013 and Idlib in 2015'); the Syria page adds that Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham later consolidated the rebel groups in 'its stronghold in northwestern Syria'.

region.text: the desert and steppe east of the Homs-Aleppo line, where the Islamic State held 'roughly two-thirds of Syria'

ledger.note: May 2015: the Islamic State at its greatest extent. The Syria page says it 'occupied roughly two-thirds of Syria by May 2015'; the Islamic State page dates the peak map to May 2015. The pages name no towns west of the Euphrates (Palmyra is not on either), so the Syrian Desert is the reading of the area. Reviewer me-10-l: region clipped to Syria (the gazetteer's Syrian Desert also takes Iraq's Anbar and Jordan's Mafraq and Ma'an, which Syria never held).

region.text: the city of Aleppo

ledger.note: 2016: the government retakes Aleppo. The '2016 victory of pro-Assad forces' in the battle for the city 'marked the recapture of what had been Syria's largest city before the war'. The page gives no day or month in the passage read.

region.text: northern Syria along the Turkish border, Aleppo province

ledger.note: August 2016: Turkey invades northern Syria. 'In August 2016, Turkey launched a multi-pronged invasion of northern Syria.' The page gives no limits; the one-cell strip of Aleppo province along the Turkish border (about 3,800 km2, drawn from the full 2006 frontier) is the reading.

region.text: Raqqa, the Islamic State's de facto capital

ledger.note: 17 October 2017: the Kurdish-led SDF capture Raqqa from the Islamic State (infobox '17 October 2017: Capture of Raqqa by SDF forces'). The land was already outside Syrian control (lost to the Islamic State in 2014); it now passes to the autonomous administration.

region.text: the Afrin district

ledger.note: January-March 2018: Turkey takes Afrin. The war page's timeline lists the 'Turkish intervention in Afrin (January-March 2018)'; Afrin is one of the autonomous administration's sub-regions.

region.text: Eastern Ghouta, the besieged rebel pocket east of Damascus (a 15 km disc round Douma cut to Syria, one cell)

ledger.note: 18 February - 14 April 2018: the government retakes Eastern Ghouta. The offensive page: 'East Ghouta, a pocket of towns and farms, had been under government siege since 2013' and 'On 14 April, the Syrian Army fully captured the Eastern Ghouta pocket'. Mirrors syrian-opposition ledger 20 (orchestrator fix, 2 Nov 2026, replacing the 80 km 'Damascus (region)' disc that took in Damascus city and Lebanese land).

region.text: Al-Baghuz Fawqani, the last stronghold, near Abu Kamal

ledger.note: 23 March 2019: the Islamic State loses its last land in Syria. Infobox: '23 March 2019: Loses all of its territory in Syria'; the text: the group 'lost their last territorial stronghold at Al-Baghuz Fawqani in Spring 2019'. Baghuz lies on the Euphrates near Abu Kamal; the land passes to the SDF-led administration.

region.text: north-eastern Syria along the Turkish border

ledger.note: September-December 2019: Turkey enters north-eastern Syria. The war page's timeline lists the 'Turkish offensive into north-eastern Syria (September-December 2019)'; the one-cell strip along the border in Raqqa and Hasakah (about 5,300 km2, drawn from the full 2006 frontier) is the reading; the page gives no limits.

region.text: Aleppo, Hama, Homs, Daraa, Sweida and Damascus, the towns taken in the offensive

ledger.note: 29 November 2024: the opposition offensive begins. 'On 29 November, rebel forces entered Aleppo'; the Syria page: 'took control of Aleppo', Hama on 5 December, Daraa and Sweida 'by 6 December', Homs 'by early morning on 8 December'.

region.text: Damascus and the land the government still held

ledger.note: 8 December 2024: the Assad government falls. 'Opposition forces captured the capital Damascus on 8 December'; 'Assad fled to Moscow with his family, where he was granted asylum'.

8 December 2024: Assad's government is replaced. A caretaker government led by Mohammed al-Bashir 'was formed the following day'; Ahmed al-Sharaa was appointed president 'for the transitional period' on 29 January 2025 (after this dossier's last year). The state, its land and its colour continue.

region.text: the UN-monitored demilitarized buffer zone (266 km2)

ledger.note: December 2024: Israel enters the Golan buffer zone. After the fall of the Assad regime 'Israeli forces entered and took control of the United Nations-monitored demilitarized buffer zone', described by Israel as a 'temporary defensive position', and later 'occupied two more Syrian villages, Jamlah and Maaraba'. No end within the dossier's years.

wars.name: Yom Kippur War
wars.outcome: Syria gained ground in the southern Golan, was pushed back to the Purple Line and then lost 500 km2 of the Bashan region to an Israeli counteroffensive; the ceasefire of 25 October 1973 was followed by the 1974 disengagement agreement that restored Quneitra and a third of the Golan.
wars.note: Fought 6-25 October 1973; the Egyptian front is in the arab-republic-of-egypt dossier.

wars.name: Syrian occupation of Lebanon
wars.outcome: Syria entered Lebanon on 31 May 1976 under the cover of the Arab Deterrent Force, took central Lebanon in October 1976, occupied the presidential palace at Baabda on 13 October 1990 and withdrew completely on 30 April 2005.
wars.note: The page is silent on any Syrian pull-back to the Beqaa after the 1982 Israeli invasion and on the Taif Agreement in its text.

wars.name: Syrian civil war
wars.outcome: Demonstrations began on 26 January 2011; rebels, the Islamic State (to 23 March 2019), the Kurdish-led administration and Turkey each took land; by 2021 the government held about two-thirds of the country; after the March 2020 ceasefire the front froze until the opposition offensive that took Damascus on 8 December 2024.
wars.note: The page does not date the SDF's founding, Palmyra, Deir ez-Zor or the 2018 Daraa operation, so none is a ledger event.

certainty.note: Judgment, not read from a page: Syria's international frontiers are treaty or armistice lines. The exceptions are the Golan (a ceasefire line from 1974, the Heights annexed by Israel in 1981 and Syria's claim unrecognised) and the Lebanese front, which is an occupation from 1976 to 2005.

From the civil war the control lines between the government, the opposition, the Islamic State, the Kurdish-led administration and Turkey are fronts, not borders; the external frontier stays as in 2010.

notes: Written by me-10-l on 2026-10-25 from six pages (one over the five-page budget: the Yom Kippur War page is shared with the Egypt dossier). WIKIDATA: Cliopatria gives Q41137 for 'Syria', which is the id of Assyria (the polities.csv row for 'assyria' has it too); the Republic of Syria rows carry Q858, which is Syria's own, and this dossier uses Q858. ONE STATE: 'Syria' (1973-2024) is the same state as republic-of-syria (1961-1966, with Ba'athist Syria), arab-socialist-ba-ath-party (1967-1972) and second-syrian-republic; the colour agent should keep one hue. The 'found' event is a row boundary (confidence 1), not a birth. GOLAN: Cliopatria's 1973 shape lacks the Golan (Israel's shape holds it); this dossier keeps it inside Syria under the occupation hatch until the 1981 law, like the predecessor. Quneitra returns in 1974 (the page also says 1975 for the buffer zone). Month of the 1974 agreement is not on the pages. THE 2014-2023 SHAPE: Syria less 64,490 km2 (60,190 km2 of it inside a 68,889 km2 outline that Cliopatria also files as 'Mujahideen' 2014-2024); the shape is frozen for ten years and does not match any dated front. Verdict adjust to the whole country, with the zones taken out year by year by the ledger. The ledger covers only what the five civil-war pages date; Palmyra, Deir ez-Zor, Daraa 2018, Quneitra 2014-2018 and the March 2020 Idlib line are not dated on them and are missing. Rebel-held land is recorded as loss/gain against slugs of dossiers that do not exist yet (syrian-opposition, islamic-state, autonomous-administration-of-north-and-east-syria). The 2017 Raqqa and 2019 Baghuz events are Islamic State to SDF transfers: they sit here only because the land stays Syrian; the rebel dossiers should own them. OCCUPATIONS WITHOUT AN END: Turkey (2016 Aleppo strip, 2018 Afrin, 2019 north-east) and Israel in the UNDOF zone (December 2024) continue past 2024; the validator warns of the unpaired starts. REGIONS TO ADD to the gazetteer: Afrin (place), and check the border_band specs and 'Syrian Desert' extent. NOT OPENED (page budget): the Lebanese Civil War, the 1974 disengagement agreement and the Hatay (Alexandretta) claim; the Syria page mentions Iskenderun only as a place Syria 'might attempt to retake'. Events after 2024 (SDF merger agreement 10 March 2025, interim constitution) are outside the dossier.
